title: RBAC v2 / Audit Pipeline: SLOs, Alert Tuning & Incident Retrospective
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a staggered rollout of RBAC v2 (role/principal format changes) we observed a degradation in audit ingestion and several auth-related latent errors that impacted downstream visibility and a subset of SSO flows. This ticket captures the incident timeline, root cause, monitoring gaps, concrete fixes applied, and follow-up actions to harden observability and alerting for auth/audit systems.

Impact:
- ~12% of audit events for RBAC changes were dropped or delayed for up to 36 hours in the ingestion pipeline (estimated 15K events).
- Affected: operator audit dashboards, compliance exports, and two customer-facing SSO sessions where role mapping failed transiently.
- Customer-facing error rate spike for SSO login success rate dropped from 99.98% to 99.60 for ~3 hours (affecting a small % of enterprise customers).

SLOs and Metrics (newly defined):
- Auth API availability: 99.95% monthly for endpoints /auth/token and /auth/verify (excl. scheduled maintenance).
- Auth latency: p95 < 120ms for token verification under normal load.
- Audit ingestion completeness: >= 99.9% of generated audit events appear in the canonical store within 10 minutes.
- Audit pipeline latency: median < 1s, p99 < 15s.
- Audit store retention and integrity: nightly checksum job completes < 30m and reports 0 mismatches.

Root Cause Summary:
- RBAC v2 introduced a new principal serialization (principal.v2.principal_id) not recognized by the audit-parser service. The parser had a strict schema and silently dropped unknown top-level fields instead of emitting structured warnings.
- The audit ingestion service continued to ack messages after partial parse; downstream indexing silently failed for those messages due to schema mismatch.
- Existing alerting focused on pipeline health (consumer lag and service errors) but not on semantic drop rates (percent of events with parsing warnings vs accepted). Deduping logic suppressed surge alerts so on-call noise was low and detection delayed.

Immediate Mitigations Applied:
- 2026-03-05 03:10 UTC: Hotfix to audit-parser deployed (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-parser/pull/1123) to accept principal.v2.* fields and emit structured warnings when unknown fields appear.
- 2026-03-05 04:00 UTC: Reingestion job started to backfill dropped events from the SQS DLQ buffer; completion by 2026-03-06 09:20 UTC.
- Temporary policy: strict-ack disabled for ingestion consumer for 24h to avoid silent drops; increased retention of DLQ to 72h.
Decisions & Trade-offs:
- We chose to relax the parser schema for forward-compatibility (adds a small risk of storing unexpected fields) to avoid availability regressions; follow-up: stricter schema validation will run in a separate job with alerting rather than blocking ingestion.
- Added an observability-focused SLO for audit completeness rather than only service-level metrics to align with compliance and customer expectations.

Monitoring & Alerting Changes (implemented):
- New metric: audit_event_parse_warning_rate (ratio of events with non-fatal parse warnings) with alert when >0.5% for 5m and >0.1% sustained for 1h.
- New metric: audit_ingestion_completeness (percentage of expected vs stored events) with pager alert at <99.5% for 30m.
- Adjusted consumer-lag alert thresholds and reduced dedupe window specifically for auth/audit streams to prevent suppression during schema transitions.
- Dashboards: created "Auth / Audit Health" dashboard in Grafana: panels for parse warnings, DLQ size, reingest progress, p50/p95 ingest latency, and event completeness heatmap. (Dashboard URL: https://grafana.redwood-inference.com/d/auth-audit-health)

Follow-up Action Items (owners & ETA):
- A1: Add canonical schema compatibility tests in CI and a canary pipeline for RBAC schema changes (owner: Marco Li, ETA: 2026-03-22).
- A2: Implement non-blocking schema validator job that writes to validation index and emits alert when validator drops >0.05% (owner: Priya Desai, ETA: 2026-03-18).
- A3: Update security runbook with SLOs and runbook steps for audit backfill (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2026-03-12) — runbook link: https://confluence.redwood-inference.com/display/SEC/Auth-Audit-Runbook
- A4: Canary deployment procedure for RBAC changes + preflight checks (owner: Platform SRE, ENG-6933, ETA: 2026-04-01).
- A5: Compliance export verification job to validate nightly exports against canonical store (owner: Data Engineering, ENG-6970, ETA: 2026-03-28).

Risks & Open Questions:
- Backfill correctness: need to validate that reingested events preserved original timestamps and ordering for ledger-style audits. Data Engineering to confirm.
- Cost: increased DLQ retention and reingestion compute will have temporary cost impact; product approves for compliance reasons.

Next Steps for this ticket:
- Review and merge remaining PRs for alerting thresholds (PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/445, https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-parser/pull/1134).
- Security review of relaxed parser schema approach (target: security council sign-off).
- Close this ticket once all action items are completed and acceptance criteria met.
